# BLASTOMYCES DERMATITIDIS

Contact Infectious Diseases in all cases. Lifelong suppressive therapy may be required in immunosuppressed patients if immunosuppression cannot be reversed.

---

## Disease outside of the central nervous system

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat for 6-12 months. It is recommended that immunocompromised patients be treated with at least 1-2 weeks of intravenous treatment and a total treatment duration of 12 months.

---

## Central nervous system infection

---

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat with intravenous therapy for 4-6 weeks followed by oral azole for at least 12 months.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat for 6-12 months. It is recommended that immunocompromised patients be treated with at least 1-2 weeks of intravenous treatment and a total treatment duration of 12 months.

References:

- Stanley et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2008, (46)1801-12
- Sanford keyword: Blastomycosis
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment of blastomycosis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Itraconazole 200 mg PO q8h for 3 days then q12h ($) [DI]

### Treatment for severe disease

Change to oral itraconazole after the patient's condition has stabilized.

### Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

Itraconazole 200 mg PO q12h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Fluconazole 400-800 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI]

### Initial intravenous treatment

### Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

Itraconazole 200 mg PO q12h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Fluconazole 800 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI]

*Local guidance (Des Moines CDSS, Inpatient):*
Amphotericin B 0.7-1 mg/kg IV q24h ($$) [R,O]
< OR >
Liposomal amphotericin (Ambisome) 3-5 mg/kg IV q24h ($$$$) [R,O]
Liposomal amphotericin (Ambisome) 3-5 mg/kg IV q24h ($$$$) [R,O]

## Outpatient

### Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Itraconazole 200 mg PO TID for 3 days then BID ($) [DI]
